summary.headline: L&T Finance posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹902 Cr (up 29% YoY) with RoA of 2.48% and credit cost easing to 2.54%.
summary.overview: Consolidated PAT hit a record ₹902 Cr, up 29% YoY, while the consolidated book reached ₹1,29,634 Cr, up 27% YoY. Retail disbursements were ₹23,852 Cr, up 36% YoY, though management said it deliberately let go of about ₹1,000–1,200 Cr of potential disbursements to protect asset quality. Credit cost moderated 10 bps sequentially to 2.54%, and NIMs + Fees was flat QoQ at 10.47%, with NIM down 24 bps offset by higher fee and other income. Management reiterated Lakshya 2031 targets (RoA 3.0–3.2%, RoE 16–18%, credit cost ≤2% over the period) and set a near-term 2.8% RoA goal for Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: up 11 bps YoY (Q4 FY26 not stated)

segments.name: Rural Business Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹6,961 Cr (up 24% YoY); book ₹32,493 Cr (up 22% YoY). Collection efficiency normalised to pre-crisis levels, and growth resumes within MFIN guardrails; Cyclops implementation planned before FY27 end.

segments.name: Farmer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹2,453 Cr (up 11% YoY); book ₹17,514 Cr (up 11% YoY). Tractor volumes were delayed in June due to late monsoon.

segments.name: Urban Finance (Two-Wheeler, Personal Loans, Mortgage)
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹10,787 Cr (up 57% YoY); book ₹63,615 Cr (up 32% YoY). Two-wheeler disbursements ₹3,006 Cr (up 41%, book ₹15,068 Cr, up 22%) with ~90% prime. Personal loans disbursements ₹4,380 Cr (up 126%, record), book ₹16,917 Cr (up 80%). Mortgage disbursements ₹3,401 Cr (up 22%), book ₹31,630 Cr (up 20%).

segments.name: SME Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹1,567 Cr (up 23% YoY) and book ₹8,884 Cr (up 28% YoY). Management self-restricted some SME cohorts due to West Asia war concerns.

segments.name: Gold Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹1,928 Cr (up 26% YoY); book ₹3,829 Cr (up 182% YoY). Branch network at 343, with ~500 new branches planned in FY27. April origination fell on new RBI tiered-loan-demand guardrails; May and June improved.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost: first target 2.0–2.2% by Q4 FY27; management said FY28 can be modelled at 2–2.2%, with Lakshya target of ≤2% over the period.

RoA: committed to 2.8% in Q4 FY27 and 3.0–3.2% by FY31; management sees ~80 bps uplift needed (≈20 bps from ARC drag fading over 2–3 years, 30–40 bps from credit and credit-administration cost efficiency, remainder from business expansion).
Cost of borrowing: Q2 FY27 may rise 5–7 bps; FY27 WACB expected at 7.35–7.40% vs 7.35% in FY26.
Gold loans expected to show normal growth trajectory in Q2 FY27; Project Hercules rollout targeted by Q3 FY27; migration of workloads to private cloud from Q3–Q4 FY27.
Surplus liquidity brought down to about ₹9,000 Cr at quarter end, described as the norm; overall liquidity was ₹13,000 Cr+ during the quarter.
capex_capacity: Gold branches: 343 at quarter end, >200 added since acquisition; plan to deploy ~500 new branches in FY27 (~1.4 per day).
Project Cyclops, Nostradamus and related projects: ~₹102 Cr cumulative spend including prior-year capitalisation, plus WIP. Cyclops alone cited at ~₹38 Cr build cost.
IT cost run-rate ₹100–120 Cr per quarter. Private cloud build-out and GPU server procurement initiated, claimed 70% cheaper than hyperscale over 5 years.
Cyclops to go live in Rural Business Finance and Mortgage during FY27; Nostradamus to extend to RBF, SME and Farm in FY27.
Project Canyon (Gold origination system) rolled out; Project Argus (SME fraud screening) launched in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Personal loans: average ticket ₹2.6–2.8 lakh; weighted average yield ~16%+ (DSA 12–13%, digital channels ~19%); four large digital partners (CRED, GPay, PhonePe, Amazon); DSA is ~10% of volumes; no FLDG arrangements; origination now largely salaried.
Gross non-starters in Personal loans below 3%; management says net non-starters are at their lowest in recent quarters.
Two-wheeler prime share ~90% of June 2026 disbursements; tractor net non-starters declining.
Management said rural collection efficiency in RBF is 99.8%.
Management stated competitive environment remains, with large banks as main Personal loan competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall while fee and other income rose, and is the NIMs + Fees trajectory sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachinn Joshi said NIM fell 24 bps to 8.54% as debt-equity rose to 3.97x from 3.73x and surplus liquidity of ~₹4,200 Cr was held; yields rose 1 bp. Surplus income was booked in fee and other income, so NIMs + Fees stayed at 10.47%.

qa_highlights.question: What guardrails govern Personal loan growth, and why were SME and Gold disbursements slower?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said PL is predominantly salaried, with Cyclops and credit parameters improving each quarter; the high growth reflects a low base. SME was cut in some cohorts due to West Asia war concerns; Gold origination fell in April on new RBI tiered-loan guardrails, with recovery in May–June.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds move, and what is the funding strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 up 5–7 bps and FY27 WACB of 7.35–7.40% vs 7.35% in FY26. Liquidity was cut to ~₹9,000 Cr at quarter end; PSL and domestic borrowing remain the main sources, with international funding deferred for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~80 bps RoA gap to Lakshya be closed, and what is the insurance commission risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said ~20 bps comes from ARC drag fading over 2–3 years, 30–40 bps from credit and credit-administration cost, and a small part from expansion. Insurance commission changes were called an industry-wide issue; payments revenue expected only after 2–2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the El Nino and monsoon risk to rural portfolio and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said rainfall was ~14% below normal as of 10 July, versus an IMD projection of ~10% deficit, with reservoirs at acceptable levels outside a few South India locations. He sees the worries as overdone, citing microfinance deleveraging from ₹4.4 lakh Cr to ₹3.3 lakh Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Is the wholesale GS3 increase a risk to credit cost, and what is the SR/ARC position?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachinn Joshi said the small GS3 rise is a settlement transition already provided for and will reverse next quarter; the rest of the wholesale book (~₹2,000 Cr) is standard. SR PCR rose to 68% from 58%; credit cost guidance excludes wholesale slippage.

qa_highlights.question: How much AI spend is variable, and what is the opex trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not give the variable AI share on the call and offered to follow up offline. Head-count efficiencies are expected to show in FY29–FY30, with the next two to three quarters not very sharp.

risks_watch: Cost of funds: management said the Q2 and FY27 WACB guidance is volatile, and declines depend on rate and liquidity conditions.
Credit cost path below 2.2% and FY28 ≤2% is unconfirmed; management said the Q4 FY27 trajectory will be the decisive check.
Monsoon and El Nino effects on Farmer and Tractor portfolios, and on rural collections.
Insurance commission regulation could hit fee income; payments business is early and unproven for profitability.
Gold and SME growth slowed in Q1 and recovery depends on the RBI tiered-loan guardrails and West Asia-linked sector stress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and Lakshya trajectory, but cautious on near-term macro: management repeatedly cited West Asia war, El Nino and monsoon volatility as reasons for prudence, and deferred FY28 credit cost and detailed AI cost answers.
key_quotes: During Q1FY27, we recorded our highest ever quarterly consolidated profit after tax of ₹902 Cr, representing a growth of 29% YoY.

We proactively tightened our credit guardrails during the quarter, deliberately letting go of about ₹1,000 Cr to ₹1,200 Cr in potential disbursements, foregoing a few percentage points of additional growth to firmly protect our asset quality.
Overall, we have spent roughly about ₹38 Cr to build Cyclops and overall we have spent roughly about ₹33 Cr for Nostradamus and ₹37 Cr for Cyclops, but the fact is that we are still in the process
But the NIMs, you can stay assured that if you looked at last almost 2.5 years and 3 years, we have been giving the guidance and we have stuck by that.

Our average yield remains at about 16% and plus, though there are certain channels which deliver, you know, again, because we operate across the spectrum, our DSA channel will probably operate at a far lower rate.

adds.what: ~500 new gold loan branches in FY27 (on top of 343 at quarter end)
Cyclops implementation to go live in Rural Business Finance and Mortgage during FY27 (IT system, not productive capacity)

growth.why: Management reiterated RoA 2.8% for Q4 FY27 and credit cost 2–2.2% by Q4 FY27 and held the 10–10.5% NIM+fees corridor; growth is backed by ~500 planned gold branches in FY27 and strong Q1 disbursements (+36% YoY), but no revenue growth guidance was given and the brief shows no explicit numeric revenue outlook.
